findings.title: Large-message streaming is required but not specified
findings.evidence: "Maximum single-message size: 4 MiB. Above this, the sender breaks the payload (e.g., large feature tree) into streamed smaller messages."
findings.problem: The spec mandates chunking for oversized payloads but defines no chunk message types, correlation fields, ordering rules, completion markers, reassembly behavior, integrity checks, or error handling.
findings.why_it_matters: Messages above 4 MiB cannot be implemented interoperably. This also conflicts with the claim that this spec defines all cross-process wire types.
findings.proposed_fix: Either define the chunked-transfer wire contract in this spec or remove streaming and require explicit rejection of any message larger than 4 MiB with a defined error code.

findings.title: Stretch tool wire types are included in the protocol without field definitions
findings.evidence: "This spec defines every type that crosses a process boundary" and "Full field definitions are deferred to stretch implementation ... the Protocol project scaffolds the record files with `// TODO: STRETCH` markers so the polymorphic registrations are complete from day one."
findings.problem: The document claims complete wire-type coverage while explicitly leaving some registered input/result records undefined.
findings.why_it_matters: Consumers cannot generate schemas, validators, or compatible serializers/deserializers for these tools. Any later field definition becomes an unstated wire-contract change.
findings.proposed_fix: Either fully specify every registered stretch tool record now or remove those types and registrations from the protocol until their fields are defined.

findings.title: Epoch rollover rule would reject the AddinReady message that announces the new epoch
findings.evidence: "A message with an `AddinSessionId` other than the current epoch is rejected with `AddinProtocolErrorMessage(ErrorCode: \"STALE_EPOCH\")`." and "The epoch changes only when `AddinReadyMessage` arrives with a new `AddinSessionId`."
findings.problem: No exception is defined for the first `AddinReadyMessage` of a new session, so the stale-epoch rule rejects the only message that can establish the new epoch.
findings.why_it_matters: Reconnects or add-in restarts are logically impossible without an unstated special case in consumers.
findings.proposed_fix: Explicitly define `AddinReadyMessage` as the only message allowed to introduce a new `AddinSessionId`, and specify how current epoch is initialized and replaced on connection/session changes.

findings.title: StateSnapshot requires Units even when there is no active document
findings.evidence: "public required UnitSystem Units { get; init; }" with nullable `DocumentId`, `DocumentType?`, `FeatureTreeHash` allowing the `"NO_DOCUMENT"` sentinel, and `required bool IsNullDocumentState`.
findings.problem: The contract requires a unit system even for null-document state, but no unit value is defined when no document exists.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementations must either invent a fake unit value or violate the contract, making null-document snapshots inconsistent across producers.
findings.proposed_fix: Make `Units` nullable in null-document state or add an explicit sentinel enum member such as `Unknown`/`None` and define when it is used.

findings.title: ToolResultMessage success/result/error invariants are not enforced anywhere
findings.evidence: `Result { get; init; } // Null when Success = false`, `Error { get; init; } // Null when Success = true`, and "Every `IToolInput` has a matching `AbstractValidator<T>`".
findings.problem: The mutually exclusive relationship among `Success`, `Result`, and `Error` exists only in comments. The validation section covers tool inputs only, not top-level messages.
findings.why_it_matters: Invalid states such as `Success=true` with `Error` populated, or both `Result` and `Error` null, remain wire-valid and leave receiver behavior undefined.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit validators and build-breaking tests for top-level message invariants, at minimum enforcing `(Success && Result != null && Error == null) || (!Success && Result == null && Error != null)`.

findings.title: ToolRegistry does not define duplicate tool-name handling
findings.location: Section 11 — Tool Registry and Schema Generation
findings.evidence: "`ToolRegistry.All` reflects the Protocol assembly ... finding every type with `[ToolName]` attributes that implement `IToolInput` or `IToolResult`." and "`ToolRegistryCompletenessTests` asserts every registered input has a matching result and vice versa."
findings.problem: The spec defines pairing but never states that each tool name must map to exactly one input type and exactly one result type.
findings.why_it_matters: Duplicate `[ToolName("...")]` annotations can create ambiguous lookups, nondeterministic schema generation, or wrong type resolution at runtime.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one-to-one uniqueness for tool names as a protocol invariant and add a build-breaking test that rejects multiple input or result types for the same tool name.

findings.title: Wire framing text conflates WebSocket frames with messages
findings.evidence: "WebSocket frame boundaries define message boundaries." and "Large messages that fragment at the WebSocket layer are reassembled by `System.Net.WebSockets` before deserialization."
findings.problem: These statements conflict. Fragmented WebSocket messages span multiple frames, so frame boundaries cannot define application message boundaries.
findings.why_it_matters: An implementer could incorrectly parse per frame, which breaks fragmented messages.
findings.proposed_fix: State that one complete JSON document maps to one WebSocket message, and explicitly say frame boundaries are irrelevant to application parsing.

findings.title: Decimal canonicalization rule is self-contradictory
findings.location: Section 8 — State Snapshot; Section 13 — Hash Canonicalization
findings.evidence: "`FeatureParameterNumber` uses `decimal` to eliminate floating-point nondeterminism in hashing. `HashCanonicalizer` serializes decimals with fixed-precision string conversion." and later "`\"G29\" format for decimal, no scientific notation`".
findings.problem: `G29` is not fixed precision and can emit exponent notation for some values, which conflicts with the stated `no scientific notation` rule.
findings.why_it_matters: Hash outputs can diverge across implementations or edge cases, undermining the determinism requirement.
findings.proposed_fix: Specify an exact decimal serialization algorithm that never emits scientific notation and add tests for extreme scales and magnitudes.

top_3_must_fix: Specify or remove the >4 MiB streaming/chunking mechanism in the wire contract.
Resolve the AddinSessionId epoch rollover contradiction so a new AddinReadyMessage can be accepted.
Remove or fully define all stretch-tool wire types before keeping them registered in the protocol.
